claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Bill Davis in 42 rounds in his American ring debut.
claims.excerpt: it took Tom just forty-two rounds to knock all the life out of Davis

claims.statement: Tom Allen lost to Charley Gallagher on Carroll Island for $2,000 a side, knocked out by a round-arm blow to the neck in the second round.
claims.excerpt: The next fight that year came off on the 23d of February, when Charley Gallagher and Tom Allen faced each other on Carroll Island for $2,000 a side.

claims.statement: Tom Allen lost to Mike McCoole at Foster's Island on 15 June 1869; referee Val McKinney awarded McCoole the stakes.
claims.excerpt: Val. McKinney thought Mike was the best man and awarded him the stakes.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Charley Gallagher at Foster's Island in 11 minutes.
claims.excerpt: On August 17 Allen turned the tables on his opponent, Charley Gallagher, in 11 minutes, at Foster's Island.

claims.statement: Tom Allen, staking $1,000 to $500, defeated James C. Gallagher on 5 November 1869 without half trying.
claims.excerpt: On November 5th, Tom Allen, staking $1,000 to $500, defeated James C. Gallagher without half trying.

claims.statement: Tom Allen and Mike McCoole were to fight for $5,000 and the championship of America on 10 November 1869, but the match fell through over a final stakeholder.
claims.excerpt: On the 10th of November, Tom Allen and Mike McCoole, who had been rematched in July, were to have fought for $5,000 and the championship of America, but they failed to agree upon a final stakeholder

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Mike McCoole on Chouteau Island in the fall of 1870 for $2,500 a side and the championship of America.
claims.excerpt: In the fall of 1870 Mike McCoole and Tom Allen met on Chouteau Island to fight for $2,500 a side and the championship of America.

claims.statement: In the Hogan-Allen fiasco, people connected with the affair were arrested by Illinois authorities after Hogan's friends let the excursion boat drift to the East St. Louis shore.
claims.excerpt: where a number of those prominently connected with the affair were arrested by the Illinois authorities

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Goss at Cincinnati.
claims.excerpt: Allen has defeated Goss at Cincinnati, and made Rooke take water at Pittsburg

claims.statement: Tom Allen made Rooke give up at Pittsburg.
claims.excerpt: Allen has defeated Goss at Cincinnati, and made Rooke take water at Pittsburg

claims.statement: Rumor said Tom Allen intended to return to St. Louis.
claims.excerpt: Rumor has it that he intends returning to St. Louis

notes: Retrospective list of St. Louis fights. Hint 'from England' for the 1878-12 travel is not in this text, so it is dropped. The Hogan-Allen fiasco names Allen but does not say what his part was. The 10 November 1869 rematch is dated here as a match that fell through, which conflicts with 093.
